how: Recruitment repeatedly asks people to save, finish, restore, grow or draw the figure.
An invitation first elicits questions identifying the group and target before a helper can join that particular effort.
Participants show the figure, report its growth and describe a previous state under griefing.
One builder specifies a nervous rather than happy figure in a white triangle above the flag.
Participants supply coordinates and a template while prospective helpers ask where the work is happening.
Speakers report beginning work before offering a bot file or seeking support, without establishing subsequent room-wide adoption.
The speaker explicitly connects starting with friends to looking for support in the same passage.
Calls can gather around work already begun, so a later building report establishes recruitment effects only when it identifies uptake of that particular call.
The call-to-building explanation requires an identifiable shared target when respondents question who the group is and where it is working.
Recruitment receives information-seeking replies that neither accept nor refuse the proposed work.
The coded invitation receives questions, while the brief reaction elsewhere does not explicitly accept a call.
A design description and target are supplied together without a documented design argument that the template settles.
A builder offers a bot file and shared target before any documented execution by helpers.
The offer and conditional encouragement do not establish whether helpers actually ran the bot or successfully held pixels.
The theme supports offering automation rather than confirmed script execution, so its running-scripts placement requires evidence of actual use.

statement: making an outside reference venue available
how: Making a chat containing a pixel reference is an observable organising step even when no transfer of decisions or discussion is visible.
Creating a reference chat establishes its availability but supports moving planning there only if the record shows that further activity.
The bot offer and unseen chat leave leadership decisions, voting and task allocation unresolved rather than demonstrating the absence of decided order.
The speaker explicitly recruits help to restore and defend an existing figure.
A restoration call and griefing update identify damaged work but do not show when repair began or whether building caused its uptake.
The participant explains hoped-for defence through simultaneous automation, but the stated mechanism remains conditional without evidence that helpers ran it.
The proposal author denies involvement in reported encroachment and disclaims control over its placers.
A loss report blames the addressed group for failing to save the figure without independently establishing responsibility.
The defence appeal and later tree dispute are not textually established as stages of the same build.
A requester appeals for restraint by asking builders to avoid a tree and pull back.
The requester invokes an asserted truce involving a third party to support the pullback appeal without establishing agreement by the builders.
Translating a truce appeal into restraint requires an addressee able to influence placers, which the responding proposal author explicitly disclaims.
The denial concerns involvement and practical control without identifying an agreement made in the room's name or disputing anyone's mandate.
The denial answers a tree request while the truce invocation is its sibling, leaving an agreement-to-authority-dispute sequence unestablished.
An unidentified group appeals to the venue for restoration help without documenting assistance received or exchanged.
The restoration appeal supplies neither evidence that another room sent help nor evidence that a shortage of hands caused that assistance.
The truce appeal and denial contain no documented exchange of help opened by border talk.
Invoking another party's truce does not establish that the builders joined a coalition.
A defence appeal and a third-party truce reference leave coalition membership and its cause unobserved.
A request to spare a tree and a denial of control do not establish host authority over an admitted guest work.
The requester names flag communities without establishing a mandate to represent either one.
Participants invoke inherited meme lore and internet history to justify representation and address potential helpers.
Meme vocabulary accompanies an accusation without establishing a pre-canvas tie naming the rival in a call to attack.
The accusation supplies no history of an earlier quarrel with the named alleged attacker.
Invoking meme lore during a build does not establish an April Fools licence for a host prank.
The broad canvas recruitment call supplies no evidence of moderation or member action containing canvas talk.
No coded response establishes that recruitment caused a boundary around canvas discussion.
A celebratory title announces the figure's presence without reporting completion or survival to the close.
Participants record destruction, vandalism and death while the placement effort remains open.
The restart report supplies a fresh start after reported loss without establishing relocation or deliberation over moving.
Fate reporting accompanies renewed building during the event rather than requiring a completed work or a post-close account.
Celebration can mark a figure's presence without a report of completion, so the completion prerequisite cannot be imposed on this announcement.
Celebration precedes a loss report in one thread without wording that makes celebration the cause of recording.
Rapid extinction and conditional encouragement do not explicitly judge the room's hands or space insufficient.
The loss and restart reports supply no explicit shortage judgement explaining a decision to move.
Restarting during open placement does not establish a decision to preserve the temporary organisation beyond the event.
The fate report and restart leave a record-driven transition to post-event organisation unobserved.
Mourning an ongoing build supplies no evidence of contest over a preserved post-close version or account.
Participants carry the placement dispute in talk through an accusation against one named community and a warning invoking another.
The requester reports encroachment on a tree without independently establishing who placed the pixels or a room-issued attack order.
The raid title names no rival target and is not textually linked to the later reported tree encroachment.
A making proposal receives a restraint request and denial, but no explicit attack call establishes the model's attack-refusal mechanism.
Reported encroachment and a truce appeal coexist in one passage without documenting an earlier attack call causing border talk.
Accusations and a warning follow reported encroachment without naming an attack call as their cause.
The brief reaction identifies neither a rival nor a finished fight, so treating it as a rival salute requires evidence the concept does not provide.
The brief reaction is preserved as its own local practice because the record does not decide whether it accepts, celebrates, concedes or salutes.
